summary_research_en: Baroque/Rococo palace built 1736-1740 and 1763-1768 by architect Bartolomeo Rastrelli for Ernst Johann von Biron, Duke of Courland; now the state Rundāle Palace Museum.
historical_owner_families: von Biron; Zubov; Shuvalov
notes: Approximate coordinates. Alternate German name "Schloss Ruhental". Partially burned by Bermontian forces 1919; restoration announced complete 2015.

name_lv: Rundāles pils franču dārzs un parks
summary_research_en: Approx. 10 ha regular French garden south of the palace, laid out by Rastrelli; tree plantings recorded to 1739, continued work during 1763-1768 construction phase.
historical_owner_families: von Biron; Zubov
notes: Approximate coordinates, same as palace. Source describes maintenance through WWI, 1930s restoration, and post-WWII sports grounds built on the parterre, but gives no present-day condition -- left null rather than assumed. Ownership plausibly shared with the palace (state) but not independently confirmed for the park itself. Hierarchy example: child of Rundāles pils.

name_lv: Rundāles pils staļļu ēku komplekss (Rietumu stallis)
summary_research_en: One of 16 buildings of the Rundāle Palace ensemble (total ensemble area 14,249.2 m²); in 2017 the state budget allocated EUR 481,090 for roof, electrical and water-pipe repairs to the western stables building.
historical_owner_families: von Biron; Zubov; Shuvalov
notes: Approximate coordinates, same as palace. Source dated 2017 described the roof as having reached "emergency state"; repairs since then were not reverified, so condition_category and current ownership are left null. Hierarchy example: outbuilding child of Rundāles pils.

summary_research_en: Neoclassical palace built 1797-1802 for Charlotte von Lieven; damaged by looting (1919) and artillery (1944), restored, and operating as a hotel since 2001.
historical_owner_families: von Lieven (Charlotte, Johann, Paul, Anatol); von Medem (tenants, late Courland period)
notes: Unresolved/unusual: transferred to the state Real Estate Agency (VNĪ) in 1996; a March 2024 article reported the state was weighing a sale of the palace. Outcome and current condition were not independently reverified.

summary_research_en: One of the largest hillforts of the ancient Semigallians, with two defensive rampart lines; most intensively settled 9th-14th century, attacked by German crusaders in 1220. First Latvian archaeological rampart backfilling carried out here in 2012 to stop erosion.
historical_owner_families: (none confirmed -- predates noble-family ownership; associated with the ancient Semigallian/Zemgaļi tribal society)
notes: Deliberately NOT linked via parent_object_id to Mežotnes pils despite physical proximity: it predates the manor by centuries and is managed/interpreted as a separate heritage trail, not part of the estate. Coordinates and municipality could not be confirmed from source.

summary_research_en: Neo-Romanesque/Art Nouveau-influenced manor house built 1901-1903 for Jelgava mayor George Armitstead; major restoration from 1976; now houses a forestry museum.
historical_owner_families: Armitstead (George Armitstead); von Brincken (from 1904); von Ungern-Sternberg (1910-1918)
notes: Source itself gives inconsistent museum-opening years (1989 in one place, 1991 in another) -- noted as a source conflict rather than picked arbitrarily. Coordinates, current condition and current legal owner could not be verified and are left null.

summary_research_en: Livonian Order castle held by the von der Recke family from 1576 to 1920 (originally granted to Matthias von der Recke, last komtur of Dobele); now converted into a hotel.
historical_owner_families: von der Recke (1576-1920)
notes: "Jaunpils pils SIA" is cited as an operating entity, but the source does not establish either current legal ownership or a current platform condition classification. Both remain null.

summary_research_en: Built from the medieval castle's outer-bailey gatehouse; rebuilt as a manor house in the 1760s, the only part of the Cēsis castle complex to undergo major renovation.
historical_owner_families: von Sievers (Count Karl Gustav von Sievers, 1830s)
notes: Shared complex coordinates. Source gives detailed ownership/condition for the adjoining medieval ruins but not separately for the New Castle building; likely shares the ruins' municipal ownership but this was not independently confirmed, so left null.

summary_research_en: Begun by the Livonian Brothers of the Sword 1208-1214, taken over by the Teutonic Order in 1237 and used as a residence of the Livonian Master; heavily damaged in the Livonian and Great Northern Wars, with conservation work beginning in the 1930s.
historical_owner_families: Livonian Brothers of the Sword / Teutonic (Livonian) Order; von Sievers (19th-century estate owners who laid out the surrounding landscape park)
notes: Explicitly owned by Cēsis Municipality per source. The ruins and Cēsu Jaunā pils belong to the same complex, but neither is a valid parent of the other; a future grouping relation may be needed.

summary_research_en: New castle built 1878-1881 for the Kropotkin family on the site of an earlier 17th-century building; damaged in WWI, rebuilt 1936-1937 under architect August Birkhans; seat of the Sigulda Region Council since 1993.
historical_owner_families: Kropotkin (Duke Dimitry and Duchess Olga); von Borch (earlier manor owners)
notes: Municipal use does not prove legal ownership, and active use does not prove a Class A condition. Both fields remain null pending authoritative verification.

summary_research_en: Medieval castle ruins visible across the Gauja valley from the New Castle; the English-language source gives almost no independent detail beyond their existence and visibility.
historical_owner_families: (none confirmed in source)
notes: Genuinely incomplete record. The medieval and new castles belong to the same complex, but the newer castle is not a valid parent of the medieval ruins.

summary_research_en: Brick castle ("Fredeland") built from 1214 for the Archbishop of Riga; abandoned after an 1776 fire, excavated from 1976 and reconstructed; part of the state Turaida Museum Reserve.
historical_owner_families: Archbishopric of Riga (territorial overlord); von Rosen and von Tiesenhausen (bailiff families); Georg Krüdener (bailiff 1514-1534); Andreas Koskul (bailiff 1560-1566)
notes: The source's "Partly restored" label does not establish that only cosmetic repairs are needed, so it cannot be mapped to Class B. Museum-reserve use also does not by itself prove legal ownership.

summary_research_en: Castle owned by the von der Osten-Sacken family until 1920, repeatedly damaged by fire (1872, 1905); public building since 1926 (municipal administration, school, cultural institution).
historical_owner_families: von der Osten-Sacken (owned until 1920; Anna Sybil von Osten-Sacken remodeled it mid-17th century)
notes: Unusual/conflicting case: the source's own infobox says "Preserved" while its body text describes severe fire damage and destroyed historic interiors -- condition_category left null rather than picking one. The builder's identity and the exact pre-1920 ownership-transfer chain are also described with uncertainty in the source itself.

summary_research_en: Neoclassical palace built 1800-1804 for the von Manteuffel family; burned in the 1905 revolution and again damaged in WWI, rebuilt 1925-1927; the Kazdanga Agricultural Trade School has occupied it since 1930.
historical_owner_families: von Manteuffel (commissioned 1800-1804; renovated by a later Baron von Manteuffel in 1907)
notes: As of Sept. 2025, the building was uninhabited and deteriorating (estimated EUR 6-7M needed for roof/heating); a residents' association had roughly one year to propose a viable future use before the municipality considers returning the building to state ownership. No single confirmed current legal owner -- left null. Referred to as both "Kazdanga Palace" (English) and "Kazdangas muiža" (Latvian), an unstandardized naming case.

summary_research_en: Manor house remodeled in the 1820s in Tukums; gifted to national poet Rainis in 1923, who owned it until his death in 1929; part of the Tukums Museum exhibition since 1991.
historical_owner_families: von Medem (Count Christoph Johann von Medem, 1818-1838); von der Recke (Baron von der Recke family, 1848-1920)
notes: Unusual provenance: personally gifted to Rainis, an unusual ownership episode for a former noble manor. Coordinates, current condition and a formal ownership category could not be confirmed and are left null.

summary_research_en: Wooden manor house built 1732 -- the oldest surviving wooden residential manor house in Latvia; owned by the von Campenhausen family until 1939; interior wall paintings by painter Georg Dietrich Hinsch; housed a school for Latvian children from 1734 to the 1890s.
historical_owner_families: von Campenhausen (owned until 1939)
notes: Current condition and ownership require authoritative verification. A separate 2024 report about seeking new operators is not the cited source and is therefore not treated as verified here.

summary_research_en: Palace built 1857-1860 for the von Pistolkors family; used as a sanatorium 1926-1995; now a hotel, restaurant and museum.
historical_owner_families: von Pistolkors (built the palace); von Mellin (family tomb monument on site)
notes: Operating as a hotel does not independently establish either legal ownership or a Class A condition; both remain null.

summary_research_en: Castle owned by the Baltic-German von Behr family from 1561 to 1920.
notes: Genuinely incomplete: the source covers ownership only up to 1920 and gives just a generic "Preserved" infobox tag with no supporting detail, and nothing on current use/ownership -- all left null rather than treating the short tag as a verified classification.

summary_research_en: Manor palace of the von Medem family (built circa 1839-1845, sources disagree on exact years); heavily damaged in WWII and rebuilt with a simplified interior; owned by the Latvia University of Life Sciences and Technologies and used as the "Vecauce" teaching/research farm.
historical_owner_families: von Medem (Count Johan Friedrich von Medem per body text; Count Karl von Medem per infobox -- source is internally inconsistent)
notes: A simplified post-war interior does not establish current cosmetic-repair needs, and university use alone is not a sufficient title check. Condition and ownership remain null. The source also conflicts on dates and the commissioning Count's first name.

summary_research_en: Castle acquired in 1529 by the House of Hochrosen/von Rosen line; passed through at least eight further owning families/entities over four centuries (including Tsar Paul I personally in 1797) before the von Rosen family repurchased it in 1857; used as a tractor workshop post-WWII and a state clinic 1963-2017.
historical_owner_families: von Rosen (House of Hochrosen, from 1529 and again from 1857); von Albedyll (1629); von Stackelberg (1704); von Lacy; von Vietinghoff; Browne; Solms and Tecklenburg counts; Tsar Paul I (1797, imperial property)
notes: The clearest multi-century, multi-family ownership chain in this sample -- a good stress-test for the historical_owner_families many-to-many relation. State clinic closed end-2017 due to building deterioration; now administered by the local municipality and opened to visitors.

summary_research_en: 19th-century manor house built for an unnamed local nobleman; expropriated in the 1920s and given to the Latvian Red Cross for a children's sanatorium; today houses the Krimulda rehabilitation hospital.
historical_owner_families: (none confirmed -- source names only an unidentified "local nobleman" as builder)
notes: Unusual current use: a former noble manor now functioning as a hospital. Hospital use does not establish legal ownership, so ownership remains null. Municipality was inferred from the 2021 administrative reform and still needs an authoritative source.

summary_research_en: One of the best-preserved medieval castles in Latvia; owned by the von Korff family from 1585 (granted by Stephen Báthory) until the 1920 agrarian reform; since 1994 houses the Jēkabpils Museum of History.
historical_owner_families: von Korff (1585-1920)
notes: "Best-preserved" and museum use do not prove the platform's Class A condition or current legal ownership. Both remain null. Included to represent eastern Latvia.

summary_research_en: Oldest surviving building in Ventspils, built in the second half of the 13th century (first written mention 1290); successively used as a Lutheran church (1706-1835), Russian Orthodox church (1845-1901) and prison (1832-1959); since 2001 houses the Ventspils Museum administration and permanent exhibition.
historical_owner_families: (none confirmed -- built and used institutionally by the Livonian Order, not a private noble family)
notes: A municipal museum can occupy a building without proving legal title, and active museum use does not prove Class A condition. Both remain null pending authoritative verification.

summary_research_en: Late Tudor Neo-Gothic palace built 1859-1863 for Baron Alexander von Fittinghof; garrisoned by the 7th Sigulda Infantry Brigade 1921-1940; now houses the Alūksne Museum.
historical_owner_families: von Fittinghof (spelling varies across sources)
notes: Unusual/disputed-name case: the owning family's name is spelled differently across sources (Fittinghof vs. Vietinghoff/Fittinghoff are plausibly transliteration variants of the same Baltic-German name). Kept as the cited source spells it rather than "corrected". Coordinates, condition and ownership category not confirmed -- left null.

summary_research_en: Livonian Order castle, held by the von Schwerin family 1573-1728 and then by the Dukes of Courland and Semigallia from 1738; a dairy operation was set up there in 1925, and the building was rebuilt for a local school in 1939.
historical_owner_families: von Schwerin (1573-1728, including Johan Ulrich von Schwerin); Dukes of Courland and Semigallia (from 1738)
notes: A 1939 school conversion does not establish current cosmetic-repair needs. Present-day condition, use and ownership remain unverified.
